title: How We Got Ridonk [with Joe Manganiello] | S2E5 "World's Greatest Couple"

sentences.en: My name is Emma, and I live in Alberta, Canada.
sentences.zh: 我叫艾玛，我住在加拿大艾伯塔省。

sentences.en: I started watching How I Met Your Mother back in high school with my first love, and we completely saw ourselves in Marshall and Lily.
sentences.zh: 我在高中时和初恋一起开始看《老爸老妈浪漫史》，当时我们完全在马歇尔和莉莉身上看到了我们自己的影子。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, like many first love situations, it ended quite painfully a few years later, and I couldn't bring myself to watch the show for a long time.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，就像许多初恋的故事一样，几年后它以相当痛苦的方式结束了，很长一段时间我都无法说服自己去看这部剧。

sentences.en: I'm 27 this year, and I decided to rewatch alongside the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我今年27岁，我决定一边听播客一边重温这部剧。

sentences.en: I haven't had much luck in love over the last 10 years,
sentences.zh: 过去10年里，我的爱情运不太好，

sentences.en: so seeing Ted start his journey at 27 and reliving all these lessons in How I Met Your Mother has really brought me back to who I am and reminded me how much is ahead of me still.
sentences.zh: 所以看到泰德在27岁时开启他的旅程，并在《老爸老妈浪漫史》中重温所有这些人生教训，真的把我拉回了真实的自我，并提醒我前方还有无限可能。

sentences.en: That line that Ted says in the limo episode, it's all important, it was all leading somewhere, was a lesson I really needed to relearn in this season of life.
sentences.zh: 泰德在加长轿车那一集里说过的那句话——这一切都很重要，这一切都有其意义——是我在这个人生阶段真正需要重新深刻理解的一课。

sentences.en: As an adult, I'm now a filmmaker, and I capture stories for a living, and it's so clear to me now how much How I Met Your Mother inspired me to pursue that path.
sentences.zh: 作为一个成年人，我现在是一名电影制作人，我以捕捉故事为生，现在我非常清楚《老爸老妈浪漫史》是如何启发我追求这条道路的。

sentences.en: The show reaches people in all kinds of chapters, and I feel so blessed that it's been with me through so many of mine.
sentences.zh: 这部剧触动了处在各种人生阶段的人们，能一路陪伴我度过这么多的岁月，我感到非常幸运。

sentences.en: I'm alone, won't be soon, in New York City, when I see you, please permit me to tell you everything, in New York City.
sentences.zh: 我很孤独，但不会太久，在纽约市，当我见到你时，请允许我告诉你一切，在纽约市。

sentences.en: Wow, what a letter.
sentences.zh: 哇，多棒的一封信啊。

sentences.en: That was amazing.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。

sentences.en: We're speechless, we've been rendered speechless.
sentences.zh: 我们说不出话来了，我们已经无言以对。

sentences.en: Welcome to another terrifically exciting episode of How We Made Your Mother.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听又一期精彩绝伦的《老爸老妈幕后故事》。

sentences.en: I'm Josh Radner, I'm with my dear friend Craig Thomas.
sentences.zh: 我是乔什·拉德诺，我和我的好朋友克雷格·托马斯在一起。

sentences.en: Hi, Craig.
sentences.zh: 嗨，克雷格。

sentences.en: Hey, Josh.
sentences.zh: 嘿，乔什。

sentences.en: We are talking about the television show How I Met Your Mother, which ran on CBS from 2005 to 2014.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈论电视剧《老爸老妈浪漫史》，它于2005年至2014年在哥伦比亚广播公司播出。

sentences.en: We're looking back, we're asking all the questions, we're remembering what it was like when we made this show, we're reflecting on it these many years later.
sentences.zh: 我们正在回顾过去，提出各种问题，回忆我们制作这部剧时的感受，并在多年后的今天对它进行反思。

sentences.en: And one of the most exciting things we're doing is hearing directly from fans, from people who have loved the show, have wrestled with the show,
sentences.zh: 我们正在做的最令人兴奋的事情之一，就是直接倾听粉丝们的心声，倾听那些热爱这部剧、纠结于这部剧的人们，

sentences.en: have rewatched the show over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 一遍又一遍、反反复复重温这部剧的人们。

sentences.en: And this letter, was it Emma, Alec, who wrote this letter?
sentences.zh: 这封信，是艾玛，还是阿历克斯写的？

sentences.en: Emma.
sentences.zh: 艾玛。

sentences.en: So beautiful.
sentences.zh: 太美妙了。

sentences.en: And one thing it reminds me of is that at any different part in your life, you can feel like a different character in the story, right?
sentences.zh: 它提醒我的其中一点是，在你生命的任何不同阶段，你都可能觉得自己是故事中的不同角色，对吧？

sentences.en: She started off feeling like she was part of the Marshall and Lily, and then she revisits 10 years later, no, I'm Ted, I'm in my Ted years.
sentences.zh: 她一开始觉得自己是马歇尔和莉莉的一部分，然后10年后她重新审视时发现，不，我是泰德，我正处于我的泰德时期。

sentences.en: I also, I noticed this while the show was on, I had a lot of women come up to me and say, I'm just like Ted.
sentences.zh: 我也有过这种感觉，我在剧集播出时就注意到了，有很多女性走来对我说，我简直就像泰德。

sentences.en: Oh, that's cool.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太酷了。

sentences.en: I like that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And I realized it had no, the gender had no bearing on where the entry point was for these things, which I really liked and appreciated.
sentences.zh: 我意识到性别与切入这些事情的角度没有任何关系，我真的很喜欢也很感激这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I love that it inspired her as an artist, too.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢它作为一个艺术家也启发了她。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That means the world.
sentences.zh: 这意义重大。

sentences.en: And I thought that, too, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 我也这么想，这很有趣。

sentences.en: You can be the Marshall and Lily in one chapter, you can be the Ted in another chapter.
sentences.zh: 你在一个章节里可以是马歇尔和莉莉，在另一个章节里你也可以是泰德。

sentences.en: Where, even as we enter season two here on this podcast, we're talking about episode five of season two here today, it's Ted and Robin have become the couple of the group.
sentences.zh: 你看，当我们在这档播客中进入第二季时，我们今天在这里讨论的是第二季第五集，泰德和罗宾已经成了群体中的情侣。

sentences.en: And Marshall and Lily are no longer the Marshall.
sentences.zh: 而马歇尔和莉莉不再是那个马歇尔了。

sentences.en: Ted and Robin are now the Marshall and Lily.
sentences.zh: 泰德和罗宾现在成了马歇尔和莉莉。

sentences.en: They're kind of functionally, like, holding down that center in the way that Marshall and Lily did.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上有点像在稳固那个核心，就像当年马歇尔和莉莉做的那样。

sentences.en: Not for long.
sentences.zh: 好景不长。

sentences.en: Not for long.
sentences.zh: 好景不长。

sentences.en: But it's, that's life.
sentences.zh: 但这就是生活。

sentences.en: That's life.
sentences.zh: 这就是生活。

sentences.en: She's making, Emma has a great observation.
sentences.zh: 艾玛的观察非常精辟。

sentences.en: It's just like, there's just these chapters, and we're all going to play all these parts at some point.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，生命中就是有这些章节，而我们终将在某个时刻扮演所有这些角色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And there's nothing that lasts forever, and it is all leading somewhere, and you do have to move through and embrace change,
sentences.zh: 没有什么东西是永恒的，这一切都有其意义，你确实必须经历并拥抱变化，

sentences.en: and also know that things will continue to change in good and bad ways.
sentences.zh: 同时也知道事情会继续朝着好的和坏的方向发生变化。

sentences.en: And that's the ride.
sentences.zh: 这就是人生之旅。

sentences.en: That's the ride that we're on.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们正在经历的旅程。

sentences.en: That's the ride of what the show is.
sentences.zh: 这就是这部剧本身的调性。

sentences.en: The other fun thing, and I'm sure people have experienced this with, like, works of art you love.
sentences.zh: 另一个有趣的事情是，我确信大家在面对自己喜爱的艺术作品时都有过这种体验。

sentences.en: Like, you love a movie as a child, or you love a movie in your teens, and you watch it 10, 20 years later, and you're different, and it's a different movie,
sentences.zh: 比如，你小时候喜欢一部电影，或者你在十几岁时喜欢一部电影，然后你在10年、20年后看它，你变了，电影也变了，

sentences.en: and your response to it is different.
sentences.zh: 而且你对它的反应也不一样了。

sentences.en: And even you might have loved it in such a way that, like, it doesn't resonate for you the same way it does in your mind.
sentences.zh: 甚至你曾经对它的爱，可能不像你记忆中那样能在内心引发同样的共鸣。

sentences.en: You know, works can take on a frequency or a resonance in our memory of them that is even stronger than how we experience them in the present.
sentences.zh: 你知道，作品在我们的记忆中可能会带有一种频率或共鸣，甚至比我们在现实中体验时还要强烈。

sentences.en: But also, a good work of art, and I think this is a testament to How I Met Your Mother being a good work of art, it changes as you change.
sentences.zh: 但同时，一部好的艺术作品——我认为这也是《老爸老妈浪漫史》是一部优秀的艺术作品的证明——它会随着你的改变而改变。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: It seems to meet you in different places, and you recognize different things the older you get.
sentences.zh: 它似乎能在不同的阶段与你不期而遇，随着年龄的增长，你会体悟到不同的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I'm grateful to Emma and anyone that has that moment that she had where the show became painful to her because of a breakup, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，我很感激艾玛以及所有那些有过她那种经历的人，因为一次分手，这部剧曾对她而言变得痛苦，对吧？

sentences.en: The thing she related to when she was younger, now that didn't, now it was painful to watch it because it wasn't that thing anymore.
sentences.zh: 她年轻时产生共鸣的东西，现在却变了，现在看它成了一种痛苦，因为它已经不再是当年的那个东西了。

sentences.en: It sounds like that she was a bit heartbroken, and now the show wasn't that comfort to her.
sentences.zh: 听起来她当时有点心碎，而这部剧不再能带给她那种慰藉。

sentences.en: The idea, I'm grateful to her that she came back around to it at this later chapter and sort of came back to it and sees new things in it.
sentences.zh: 但这个想法是……我很感激她在后来的这个阶段重新回来看这部剧，算是再次接触并从中看到了新的东西。

sentences.en: But that's really cool, and I'm honored when fans do that.
sentences.zh: 但这真的很酷，当粉丝们这样做时，我感到非常荣幸。

sentences.en: And I think that is, yeah, I have so many movies and shows and books and things that I go back to, and it's like, I have a completely different experience.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，是的，我有那么多的电影、剧集、书籍以及各种东西，当我回过头去重温时，就好像拥有了完全不同的体验。

sentences.en: The next time I read it 5, 10, 15, 20 years later, The Great Gatsby is always different.
sentences.zh: 5年、10年、15年、20年之后我再次阅读，情况总是不同，《了不起的盖茨比》每一次都不一样。

sentences.en: You go back to these things, you go, this meant so many different things to me at so many different points.
sentences.zh: 当你重新审视这些事物时，你会发现，在不同的时间点，它们对我有着完全不同的意义。

sentences.en: And that really is cool.
sentences.zh: 这真的很酷。

sentences.en: That is the cool thing about art.
sentences.zh: 这就是艺术最酷的地方。

sentences.en: So, we are talking today about episode 5 of season 2.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们今天在聊的是第二季第5集。

sentences.en: The name of this episode and the air date, Alec, this is your big moment.
sentences.zh: 这一集的名称和播出日期，亚历克，这是你的高光时刻。

sentences.en: This is the moment we wait for every week for you to pop in and remind us when this show aired.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们每周都在等待的时刻，等你跳出来提醒我们这部剧是什么时候播出的。

sentences.en: No pressure.
sentences.zh: 没有压力哦。

sentences.en: Okay, sorry, let me just look it up.
sentences.zh: 好吧，抱歉，让我查一下。

sentences.en: Hold on one second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: You already have one job, Alec.
sentences.zh: 亚历克，你本来就只有一件工作。

sentences.en: You have one job.
sentences.zh: 你只有这一件工作。

sentences.en: You know what, you actually have like 100 jobs, so we should...
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，其实你大概有一百件工作，所以我们应该……

sentences.en: I have a lot of tabs open.
sentences.zh: 我开了好多标签页。

sentences.en: We are talking about The World's Greatest Couple, which first aired on October 16th in 2006, written by Brenda Shea.
sentences.zh: 我们要聊的是《世上最伟大的一对》，它于2006年10月16日首播，由布伦达·谢伊编剧。

sentences.en: Brenda Shea, on the show for three years, very talented, funny writer.
sentences.zh: 布伦达·谢伊，在这部剧工作了三年，非常才华横溢、幽默风趣的编剧。

sentences.en: And I remember her being...
sentences.zh: 我记得她……

sentences.en: She was always very good at writing Barney.
sentences.zh: 她一直非常擅长写巴尼的戏份。

sentences.en: Brenda wrote Barney really well.
sentences.zh: 布伦达把巴尼写得太棒了。

sentences.en: She always enjoyed that.
sentences.zh: 她一直很享受这一点。

sentences.en: She had a lot to do with that Lemon Law episode in season 1.
sentences.zh: 第一季里那个“柠檬法”的那集，她出了很多力。

sentences.en: And she's a very funny writer, and I always felt like she took to Barney in that same way that some women relate to Ted watching it.
sentences.zh: 她是一位非常搞笑的编剧，我总觉得她对待巴尼的方式，就跟有些女性看剧时对特德产生共鸣一样。

sentences.en: I'm Ted Mosby.
sentences.zh: 我就是特德·莫斯比。

sentences.en: Brenda had a...
sentences.zh: 布伦达有一个……

sentences.en: But by the way, Brenda's nothing like Barney in real life.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，布伦达现实生活中一点也不像巴尼。

sentences.en: That was not my experience of her.
sentences.zh: 我从她身上可没看到这种感觉。

sentences.en: No, no, she's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不，她不是。

sentences.en: I don't mean it like that, but as a writer, she wrote very funny stuff for Barney.
sentences.zh: 我不是那个意思，但作为编剧，她为巴尼写的内容真的非常搞笑。

sentences.en: So we have a very special guest who will be joining us in a bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有一位非常特别的嘉宾，等一会儿就会加入我们。

sentences.en: But before we get to that, we're going to talk a little bit about other parts of the episode.
sentences.zh: 但在我们进入正题之前，我们要先聊聊这一集的其他部分。

sentences.en: But Craig, just give us a quick summary of what happens in this episode.
sentences.zh: 不过克雷格，请给我们简单总结一下这一集发生了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a play on couplehood, this episode.
sentences.zh: 好的，这一集其实是在玩转“伴侣关系”这个概念。

sentences.en: There are a couple of strange bedfellows, and that's actually literally true with the way the episode begins.
sentences.zh: 里面出现了一些奇怪的组合，从这一集开场的方式来看，字面意思确实如此。

sentences.en: Barney and Lily are in bed in the beginning of the episode, and it's one of those, let's show how we got here.
sentences.zh: 巴尼和莉莉在剧集开头时躺在床上，这就是那种“让我们倒叙看看我们是怎么走到这一步的”的情节。

sentences.en: So Lily has this dilemma of her apartment is horrible.
sentences.zh: 所以莉莉遇到了一个难题，她的公寓太糟糕了。

sentences.en: The apartment, she came back from San Francisco, she has a horrible apartment, she needs somewhere better to live.
sentences.zh: 她从旧金山回来后，租了一套糟糕的公寓，她需要找个更好的地方住。

sentences.en: She turns to Barney, she becomes Barney's roommate.
sentences.zh: 她求助于巴尼，成了巴尼的室友。

sentences.en: He's very reluctant until he realizes that she can help him by chasing away one night's fans by pretending to be his wife, coming home and discovering them together.
sentences.zh: 他一开始很不情愿，直到他意识到莉莉可以假装是他的妻子回家并当场抓包他们，以此来帮他赶走那些只留宿一晚的狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: And our other funny couple of the episode is Marshall and Brad with our very special guest who will be on in a few minutes, Joe Manganiello, who's hilarious in this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们这集的另一对搞笑搭档是马歇尔和布拉德，还有我们几分钟后就会登场的特别嘉宾乔·曼根尼罗，他在这一集里搞笑极了。

sentences.en: And just a great dude, and just super funny.
sentences.zh: 他真是个绝佳的家伙，超级搞笑。

sentences.en: And the two of them together, both recently heartbroken lamenting that they've lost all of these things they love to do, like brunch, because they're not in couples anymore,
sentences.zh: 他们两个最近都刚失恋，感叹着自己失去了所有喜欢做的事，比如早午餐，因为他们不再是情侣了，

sentences.en: that's the other big part of this.
sentences.zh: 这就是另一大重点。

sentences.en: And then Ted and Robin, again, they're the new Marshall and Lily, they're sort of holding it down, just kind of laughing at everybody else a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后是泰德和罗宾，他们俩又成了新一代的马歇尔和莉莉，他们算是在维持大局，顺便对其他所有人略带嘲笑。

sentences.en: The way that a couple that is comfortable together is like, at least none of this shit's happening to us.
sentences.zh: 那种合拍的情侣会有的心态就像是，至少这些狗屁倒灶的事没发生在我们身上。

sentences.en: Quietly disdainful of everyone's missteps and adventures.
sentences.zh: 默默地对每个人的失误和冒险表示不屑。

sentences.en: They're Statler and Waldorf Muppets.
sentences.zh: 他们就是布偶秀里的老头子斯塔特勒和沃尔多夫。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: Up in the balcony, kind of enjoying everyone's pain a little bit.
sentences.zh: 坐在楼上的包厢里，多少有点幸灾乐祸地看着大家的痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, Craig, we talk so much about how the whole, all of How I Met Your Mother is one big mystery in the title.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，克拉格，我们经常讨论整部《老爸老妈浪漫史》剧名里包含的那个巨大的悬念。

sentences.en: How did this happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: How did he meet?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么遇到的？

sentences.en: But each, there's many episodes that are mysteries.
sentences.zh: 但每一集里，其实都有很多悬念。

sentences.en: They start off as a mystery.
sentences.zh: 它们都是从一个悬念开始的。

sentences.en: This episode literally starts, what is this craziness?
sentences.zh: 这一集的开场简直就是，这到底是什么疯狂的情况？

sentences.en: Lily and Barney are in bed together.
sentences.zh: 莉莉和巴尼躺在同一张床上。

sentences.en: How the hell did this happen two weeks earlier?
sentences.zh: 两周前到底怎么会搞成这样？

sentences.en: You know, classic kind of like, start at the end and work your way towards and show how this happened.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是一种经典套路，从结局开始，然后倒叙回去，展示这一切是如何发生的。

sentences.en: And also, it's a misdirect.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是个烟雾弹。

sentences.en: It's not what you think.
sentences.zh: 事情并不是你想的那样。

sentences.en: They, you know, they did not sleep together.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们并没有睡在一起。

sentences.en: But, well, they slept next to each other.
sentences.zh: 不过，好吧，他们挨着对方睡了。

sentences.en: So many of our best episodes have some mini mystery in them.
sentences.zh: 我们许多最棒的剧集里面都包含一些微型悬念。

sentences.en: That's the thing that's hitting me the most in this rewatch.
sentences.zh: 这是我在这次重温中最深有体会的一点。

sentences.zh: 就像，我记得当我们把那个床拉下来结果它卡住的时候。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 就有点，呃，你知道的，做出了那种反应，我知道那不是，我知道，我，我每次做出的反应都不一样。

sentences.zh: 因为那真的，似乎有一种合法的危险，就好像它可能会失控一样。

sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们的制作团队那么优秀。

sentences.en: There's really, there was, there was some physics at work there and I can see that hitting a real, having a real response, you know?
sentences.zh: 那里真的，有，有一些物理原理在起作用，我能理解那种冲击，能产生真实的反应，你知道吗？

sentences.zh: 看起来太棒了。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 他的作品总是在《纽约客》上发表。

sentences.zh: 我和他挺熟的，他把他的书寄给了我。

sentences.zh: 他把他的第一本书寄给了我，呃，书名叫作《这就是我》。

sentences.en: And then, then he, there's a sequel that I, that I was delighted to come home, uh, last night and discover he'd sent to me.

sentences.en: So I spent this morning reading, uh, the second book of cartoons and they're so funny.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天早上一直在读，呃，第二本漫画书，它们太搞笑了。

sentences.en: Shout out to Asher Perlman.
sentences.zh: 向阿舍·珀尔曼致敬。

sentences.en: And worth, well worth picking up a copy and giving it to your friends.
sentences.zh: 而且非常值得买一本送给你的朋友。

sentences.en: But, um, the, the guy who was on the other side of the wall that was ripped looks so much like an Asher Perlman character.

sentences.en: Like, it's unbelievable.

sentences.en: There's people in these cartoons that are like, that's the guy.
sentences.zh: 这些漫画里有些人就像是，那就是那个人。

sentences.en: That's the guy.
sentences.zh: 就是那个人。

sentences.en: He had a great look, that guy.
sentences.zh: 那家伙长得很有特点。

sentences.en: It's not that Asher Perlman's, uh, his cartoons look like cartoons.
sentences.zh: 倒不是说阿舍·珀尔曼的，呃，他的漫画看起来像漫画。

sentences.en: That guy looked like a, like a, like someone drew him, you know?
sentences.zh: 那家伙看起来像个，像个，就像有人画了他一样，你知道吗？

sentences.en: He was unbelievable, the character behind that wall.
sentences.zh: 他太不可思议了，墙后面的那个角色。

sentences.en: It really made me laugh because I had, I, I, I read the whole book and then watched the episode.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我大笑，因为我，我，我读完了整本书，然后看了那一集。

sentences.en: And I was like, how did an Asher Perlman character get into the episode 2006 of How I Met Your Mother?
sentences.zh: 然后我就想，阿舍·珀尔曼笔下的角色怎么会跑到2006年播出的《老爸老妈的浪漫史》那一集里？

sentences.en: See, it changes over time.
sentences.zh: 你看，这是会随着时间改变的。

sentences.en: Like we were saying in the opening, we change this as you change.
sentences.zh: 就像我们在开场时说的，随着你的改变，我们也会改变。

sentences.en: Full circle.
sentences.zh: 完美闭环。

sentences.en: Um, but no, I did want to talk about, um, the, another great, another wonderful, wonderfully constructed shot by our wonderful director and camera crew, which is that reveal,
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过说真的，我确实想谈谈，嗯，另一个伟大的，另一个精彩的，由我们出色的导演和摄影组精心构建的长镜头，也就是那个揭晓，

sentences.en: right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: I was talking to you guys before we recorded about that reveal that is a Coen Brothers shout out.
sentences.zh: 我们在录制前跟你聊过那个致敬科恩兄弟的揭晓镜头。

sentences.en: Can I talk about that for a second?
sentences.zh: 我能稍微聊聊这个吗？

sentences.en: Please.
sentences.zh: 请便。

sentences.en: Uh, I've been, I've been raring to get to this and no one will care or know what I'm talking about, but I'm just going to do it anyway because it makes me happy.
sentences.zh: 呃，我一直，我一直急着想聊这个，虽然没人会在乎或者知道我在说什么，但我还是要说，因为这让我开心。

sentences.en: In the movie Miller's Crossing, which is one of my favorite films and Carter too, there's this moment where Tom Regan, who's played by Gabriel Byrne, enters his own apartment,
sentences.zh: 在电影《米勒的十字路口》里，这是我最喜欢的电影之一，卡特也很喜欢，有这样一个场景：由加布里埃尔·伯恩饰演的汤姆·里根进入他自己的公寓，

sentences.en: comes down, the phone's ringing, it's late at night.
sentences.zh: 走进来，电话在响，已经是深夜了。

sentences.en: He sits down, answers the phone, and you're just tight on Gabriel Byrne, and he has an entire phone call, hangs up the phone, and he's,
sentences.zh: 他坐下，接起电话，镜头一直紧紧对准加布里埃尔·伯恩，他打完了一整通电话，挂断电话，然后他，

sentences.en: the whole time he's looking kind of past camera, you're right in his face, and then he hangs up the phone and he goes, hello, Bernie.
sentences.zh: 全程他都把目光投向镜头之外，你就在他脸特写上，接着他挂断电话说，你好，伯尼。

sentences.en: Bernie, and you reveal that that entire time, Bernie Byrnebaum, John Turturro, was sitting, had broken into his apartment and was sitting there,
sentences.zh: 伯尼，然后镜头揭晓，原来这整段时间里，由约翰·特托罗饰演的伯尼·伯恩鲍姆一直坐在那里，闯入了他的公寓并坐在那儿，

sentences.en: and there's this incredibly ominous reveal because it's definitely trouble that this guy is sitting there, and it just, you're so long just on Tom Regan and Gabriel Byrne,
sentences.zh: 这个揭晓非常有不祥的预感，因为这家伙坐在那儿绝对意味着麻烦，而且，镜头在汤姆·里根和加布里埃尔·伯恩身上停留了那么久，

sentences.en: and then all of a sudden it's this reveal after a long phone call that Bernie's there.
sentences.zh: 然后在一通冗长的电话之后，突然揭晓伯尼其实一直都在。

sentences.en: Well, that's exactly what we did with Barney.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这正是我们对巴尼的处理方式。

sentences.en: Barney walks in, he's on his earpiece, he's having this long phone call, having this, like, angry, like, threatening call that turns out to be with his own mother,

sentences.en: and then after a really long cross, only on him, you reveal, and it's all in one shot, which is not true in the Miller's Crossing, but it's all in one shot,
sentences.zh: 而在进行了非常久的全景追踪、镜头只对着他一个人之后，谜底揭晓了，而且这一切都是一镜到底，虽然《米勒的十字路口》里并非如此，但这全是一镜到底，

sentences.en: The Coen brothers don't know how to move a camera, that's what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 科恩兄弟根本不懂怎么运镜头，这就是我想说的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: You know, it's also a great thing when you're an artist, you watch movies and you read books, and we've talked so much about all the crazy kind of influences,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你是一个艺术家时，这也很棒，你看电影，读书，我们已经讨论了很多关于各种疯狂的影响，

sentences.en: and even on subtle levels, you know, when you're doing things, you might not even realize you're paying homage.
sentences.zh: 甚至在潜移默化的层面，你知道，当你做事的时候，你可能甚至没有意识到自己在致敬，

sentences.en: to something, or ripping it off outright, but it's so much fun to have a vocabulary, you know, to have a vocabulary to talk about these things, and speak in shorthand with,
sentences.zh: 某样东西，或者纯粹是抄袭，但拥有一套话语体系是多么有趣，你知道，拥有一套谈论这些事情的话语体系，并用简写与，

sentences.en: you know, a DP, or, you know, who might have the same references.
sentences.zh: 你知道，摄影指导交流，或者，你知道，可能有着相同参考对象的人交流。

sentences.en: I did, it really amused me that, you know, Barney was placing bets, and then he's threatening, and it turns out it's his mom, but I also, you know, we talked in episode two about,

sentences.en: like, this compulsive, kind of addictive quality of Barney, and it's like, yeah, of course he's cross-addicted, and he's a gambler.
sentences.zh: 就像巴尼身上这种强迫性的、成瘾的特质，就好像，对，他当然有多重瘾症，他是个赌徒。

sentences.en: Like, he's got bets going everywhere, you know, like, of course, that's just, like, a natural extension.
sentences.zh: 就像，他到处都在下注，你知道，就好像，这只是，像是一种自然的延伸。

sentences.en: It's on brand.
sentences.zh: 这很符合他人设。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.zh: 你知道，这个，还有，莉莉和巴尼的这条故事线让我想起了，我想是格雷格，也可能是乔纳森·格罗夫，

sentences.en: I can't remember who said this to me, but, you know, you've got something good when you can picture any two characters in a scene,

sentences.zh: 对，我觉得那是玛琳的风格。

sentences.zh: 这有点像，再次说明，编剧会想，如果，哦，对，如果莉莉没地方住，然后最后和巴尼住在一起，

sentences.en: What happens?
